profile_text.body:
The AI Now Institute is a nonprofit founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York, NY. On its website, the institute describes itself as challenging and reimagining the current trajectory for AI. It publishes an annual report that, according to the site, maps the state of play with the AI market, interrogates the industry's key sources of power, and provides an actionable strategy to reclaim public agency over the future of AI.

The site quotes Heidy Khlaaf, the institute's chief AI scientist and a former OpenAI safety engineer, saying that ordinary security engineering would have stopped the OpenAI hack well short of reaching Hugging Face's data, and that scientific claims require falsifiability. Sarah Myers West, co-executive director, is quoted discussing whether agentic supreme intelligence is possible, the responsibility companies have in developing AI tools, and what politicians need to do to get up to speed on the technology.

The available record lists no products for the institute and no litigation cases. It does list 458 New York law exposure entries for the organization.
